channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Kroll CEO: Borrower Quality on New Deals Remain Firm
item.description: Kroll CEO, Jacob Silverman, discusses the state of private markets, noting that their previous conversation in April or May covered concerns and growing pains in the sector. Silverman discusses the firm’s perspective as one of the largest valuation agents in private markets and asks whether anything has changed over the past four or five months. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cisco President on Defending Against AI Attacks
item.description: Jeetu Patel, Cisco’s President and Chief Product Officer, discusses an open letter signed by Cisco, OpenAI, Anthropic and others warning that AI-enabled cyberattacks are likely to become more widespread and sophisticated. He says the same tools that help people work more efficiently can also help bad actors operate at machine scale. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Indian Workers Are Helping Train the Robots That Will Replace Them
item.description: On today’s Big Take Asia podcast: How Indian workers are using iPhones to train humanoid robots and what the race for real-world data means for the future of work.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Choong Wilkins and Yang Yang

item.title: Marquee Brands CEO on Roots Acquisition, Brand Building
item.description: Heath Golden, CEO of Marquee Brands, discussed the company’s planned acquisition of Canadian outdoor and lifestyle brand Roots, calling it a strong fit with Marquee’s strategy of buying timeless, high-awareness brands with room to grow. Golden said Marquee is building a portfolio of about 24 brands, including Martha Stewart, Roberto Cavalli, Ben Sherman and BCBG, and sees Roots as another brand with strong consumer love and broad permission to expand by category and geography. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Tyler Kendall on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bitcoin Hack, AMC-Robinhood Feud, Awaiting CLARITY | Bloomberg Crypto 9/8/2026
item.description: "Bloomberg Crypto" covers the people, transactions, and technology shaping the world of decentralized finance. Today's guests: AVA Labs Vice President of OnChain Finance Morgan Krupetsky, BitGo Co-Founder & CEO Mike Belshe, Coinbase Vice Chair & Head of Corporate Affairs Ryan VanGrack, and WalletConnect CEO Jess Houlgrave. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Qualcomm CFO on Amazon AI Chip Deal, Data Center Strategy
item.description: Qualcomm CFO Akash Palkhiwala discusses the company's deal to create customized chips for Amazon Web Services’ AI infrastructure. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Palkhiwala also comments on Qualcomm's AI data center strategy and the future of smartphones. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Binance Keeps Doing European Business Without License
item.description: Bloomberg's Ben Weiss joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Despite failing to get a license in Europe, it's business as usual for Binance in Europe. The firm is still operating in the region due to a number of workarounds and side doors under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulatory framework, better known as MiCA. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New Bitcoin Hack Exposes Cracks In Crypto
item.description: Bloomberg Intelligence's Dushyant Shahrawat, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." A blockchain used by several cryptocurrency exchanges to move Bitcoin was hacked for $320 million, the latest in a spate of breaches to shake confidence in digital-asset security. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: If Clarity Fails, Growth Goes Offshore: Houlgrave
item.description: Jess Houlgrave, CEO of WalletConnect, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discus the importance of the Clarity Act and how regulation affects her business. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: We Are More Than Just Crypto: Coinbase's VanGrack
item.description: Ryan VanGrack, vice chair and head of corporate affairs at Coinbase, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss Coinbase taking the first regulatory step toward letting US investors make leveraged, round-the-clock bets on stocks without owning them. VanGrack also talked about US regulation and Anthony Armstrong joining Coinbase. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple to Unveil First Foldable Phone
item.description: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said that the foldable phone expected to be announced by Apple this week has been 'a long time coming' for the company after Tim Cook took inspiration from similar phones he saw on a 2020 trip to Asia. Gurman said that the stakes for Apple's new product releases are high because every issue a new product has could be detrimental to the brand and its reputation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Not A Conclusion We Lose World Liberty Business: Belshe
item.description: Mike Belshe, co-founder & CEO of BitGo, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." A company tied to World Liberty Financial, the Trump family’s crypto venture, received preliminary conditional approval for a national trust bank charter from a federal regulator. It would no longer need its current issuer BitGo Bank & Trust. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Announces Muse AI Agent for Personal Tasks and Organization
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. unveiled a new artificial intelligence agent designed to carry out tasks on a user’s behalf, advancing Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of a future where people each have a personalized AI assistant.
item.dc:creator: Riley Griffin

item.title: Legislative Path Required To Go Forward: Belshe
item.description: Mike Belshe, co-founder & CEO of BitGo, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss the need for the passage of the Clarity Act in the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Truist Adds to Investment Bank With Insurance, Healthcare Hires
item.description: Cem Altuntas is joining Truist Financial Corp.’s investment bank as head of insurance brokers and services as the regional bank builds out its advisory business.
item.dc:creator: Matt Monks

item.title: Canada Tariffs Escalate Trade Spat; Markets brace for Inflation Test
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Vonnie Quinn and Bailey Lipschultz on "Bloomberg Open Interest." The summer calm may be over. Middle East tensions hit markets ahead of a crucial inflation report, as the US-Canada trade fight escalates. Apple enters the John Ternus era with a foldable iPhone. Plus, NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell on racing’s momentum, Bloomberg Intelligence’s Mandeep Singh on Qualcomm’s Amazon chip deal, and Julie Macklowe on tariffs, whiskey and the rise of ready-made cocktails. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Evolution’s Compliance Checks Faulty, Unsealed Report Says
item.description: Evolution AB had “ineffective” compliance procedures for checking if its casino games were accessible in markets where gambling is illegal, according to a 2022 report made public in a Tuesday court filing.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Solon

item.title: UK to Make Apple, Google Block Nude Images on Kids’ Devices
item.description: The UK government will require technology companies such as Apple Inc. and Google to stop children from taking, sharing or viewing nude images on their phones and tablets, Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy told the House of Commons on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Reid

item.title: Qualcomm Lands Amazon as Customer for Push Into AI Chips
item.description: Qualcomm Inc. signed up Amazon.com Inc. as a data center chip customer and investor, scoring a major win in its bid to benefit from soaring artificial intelligence spending.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Farmers Embrace AI More Than Any Other Tech, McKinsey Says
item.description: Artificial intelligence use is surging on farms as growers look for some high-tech help in planning and managing operations after years of scaling back on spending, according to McKinsey & Co.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hirtzer
